correctness.rationale: The proof derives \(N_k(q)=q^{k^2-k}\) from a unique Fitting decomposition, then conditions on rank \(r\) to get \(q^{n^2-r}\) good second matrices. Averaging kernel sizes gives \((2q^n-1)/q^{2n}\). Nilpotent ideals preserve nilpotency under projection, and Wedderburn factors of the finite radical quotient yield the product formula. The extremal bound and noncommutative example follow. Explicit exhaustive verification of five full matrix cases and three additional finite rings matched all counts, without using finite tests as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recent 2026 probability literature explicitly motivates extension beyond commutative and triangular rings. This theorem computes the exact probability for every finite associative unital ring using only its Wedderburn factors, gives a surprising match between full matrix rings and corresponding extension fields, and classifies all sharp maximizers including genuinely noncommutative local rings. This is a complete natural family, not a narrow arbitrary sample or a mere re-expression of a single finite table.
